decision_reason: Two sources jointly document reduced benefit access and materially higher emergency-food demand in Arizona.

event_assessment.attribution: 12News reported near-doubled food-box demand at St. Vincent de Paul, while the Arizona Food Bank Network documented historically elevated food-bank need.

measurable_change.description: St. Vincent de Paul in Phoenix is experiencing sharply increased demand for emergency food boxes as hundreds of thousands of Arizonans have lost SNAP access. The provider's own current materials corroborate the underlying strain: families now seeking assistance include people who were not seeking help six months earlier, some applicants face benefit-system delays exceeding a month, and its twice-monthly drive-through food distribution operates only until available food is exhausted.
measurable_change.measurement: food bank network condition: Arizona Food Bank Network reports that food-bank visits have been increasing and began outpacing SNAP participation in late 2025.; food bank need condition: The network reports that people need food banks more than at any point in the previous 10 years.; current snap tracker url: https://www.cbpp.org/research/food-assistance/snap-tracker-people-are-losing-food-assistance-as-the-harmful-2025; current snap tracker updated at: 2026-08-26

event_assessment.organization: Society of St. Vincent de Paul Phoenix
event_assessment.service: SNAP food assistance and emergency food-box distribution.

causal.note: Food-bank visits are service encounters rather than a count of unique households and should not be compared one-for-one with SNAP enrollment. Arizona SNAP participation has partially rebounded from its May 2026 low, although it remains substantially below July 2025 levels. The reviewed evidence does not establish what share of the SNAP decline reflects changed eligibility, administrative barriers, economic changes or other causes. The reviewed sources do not establish the exact current number of food boxes available per distribution, the number of households turned away after supplies are exhausted, whether every recent distribution has run out, or the precise baseline period used by 12News for the reported near-doubling in demand. The finding therefore establishes substantial current capacity pressure but not a quantified service shortfall.

publication_copy.headline: Phoenix food-box demand rose as Arizona SNAP access contracted
publication_copy.summary: St. Vincent de Paul in Phoenix reported that demand for food boxes had nearly doubled as Arizona food-bank visits rose and SNAP access contracted; the sources did not establish a precise turnaway count or causal split.

recommended_batch.edition_introduction: This retrospective documents August benefit-access contractions and the emergency-food demand reported alongside them, while preserving the limits of the available evidence.
